# PreserveYourEstate.com

> Preserve Your Estate (preserveyourestate.com) is the educational website of MSA Financial, LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser in Braintree, Massachusetts (CRD #107768). SEC registration does not imply a certain level of skill or training.

> Educational content about Massachusetts estate and tax planning coordination. Michael Cammarata, CFP®,
> is Managing Partner and Owner at MSA Financial, LLC (SEC-registered RIA, CRD #107768,
> established 1997, approximately $1.5B in client assets as of August 12, 2026). Offices: Braintree,
> Sandwich, and Framingham, MA. Topics include the Massachusetts estate tax (M.G.L. c. 65C),
> credit shelter (A/B) trusts, QTIP trusts, trust funding, and retirement planning questions for
> Massachusetts households with $2M or more in investable assets. All offices: (781) 843-3500.
> Michael is not an attorney or CPA. He does not draft legal documents, provide legal or tax
> advice, or prepare tax returns. He coordinates with clients' independent estate attorneys and CPAs.
> All content is educational only and is not individualized legal, tax, or investment advice.

## Key facts (verified October 28, 2026; rules may change)
- For Massachusetts residents dying on or after January 1, 2023, a Massachusetts estate tax return is required when the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts exceeds $2,000,000, and a credit of up to $99,600 applies. Source: Massachusetts Department of Revenue, Estate Tax Guide (updated April 23, 2026): https://www.mass.gov/info-details/estate-tax-guide
- The Estate Tax Guide describes no spousal portability election for the Massachusetts estate tax. The federal basic exclusion amount is $15,000,000 for 2026 (IRS): https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/whats-new-estate-and-gift-tax
- Massachusetts 4% surtax applies to taxable income above $1,107,750 for tax year 2026. Source: Massachusetts Department of Revenue (page updated June 1, 2026): https://www.mass.gov/info-details/massachusetts-4-surtax-on-taxable-income
- Illustrative estate tax figures are available on the calculator page. They are educational estimates, not tax advice. A CPA calculates any actual tax.
